title: Three things I got wrong about calibration
thesis: Calibrate before trusting the scanner, but for better reasons than the three I gave.

nodes.text: Calibration is not a one-time job; bands drift as the corpus grows.

evidence.filled_by: a lock: a named snapshot calibrated against on purpose

nodes.text: Shipped thresholds are guesses, and a labelled guess beats an unlabelled measurement.

evidence.filled_by: the UNCALIBRATED banner drove more calibration than argument did

nodes.text: A banner that never goes away stops being read; it must change when the corpus is thin.
Five samples give bands but not bands you should trust.

evidence.filled_by: the tool now says 'thin' below ten

nodes.text: The tool was right; the reasons were the weak part.
